titleEn: How Game Lighting Began: From DOOM to Deferred Rendering
descriptionKo:
게임의 빛은 어떻게 시작됐을까요? 둠의 구역 밝기부터 퀘이크의 라이트맵, 법선과 그림자, 포워드·디퍼드 렌더링까지 연결합니다.

실제 게임 화면과 언리얼 엔진의 개발 시연을 검정 배경의 2.5D 도식·작은 계산 예제와 함께 살펴봅니다. 가시성과 조명을 구별하고, 무엇을 미리 저장하는지, 실행 중에는 어떤 값을 읽고 계산하는지 설명합니다.

게임 렌더링 이야기 1편입니다. 시연 화면에서 직접 보이는 결과와 내부 구현에 대한 설명을 구별합니다.

descriptionEn:
How did lighting in games begin? This episode connects DOOM’s sector brightness to Quake lightmaps, normals, shadows, forward and deferred shading, and SSAO.

We combine actual game footage and Unreal Engine development demonstrations with animated 2.5D diagrams and worked examples. Learn to separate visibility from lighting, identify what is stored in advance, and follow the data read and calculated at runtime. Visible results are distinguished from claims about internal implementation.

Part1 of our game-rendering series.

00:00 Introduction: stored and computed lighting
00:26 Visibility versus lighting
03:30 DOOM: sector brightness and palettes
04:54 Quake: lightmaps and baking
08:55 Texture filtering and mipmaps
11:38 Tile-based GPUs
13:02 DOOM3: normals and shadow volumes
15:26 Half-Life2: directional lightmaps and spatial samples
23:44 Shadow maps and depth comparison
25:39 Cascaded shadow maps
27:52 Forward and deferred shading
33:35 SSAO: occlusion from screen depth
35:30 Summary: what is stored, and when is it computed?
36:13 Thank you to our members
